concepts.def: Camus's novel narrated by Meursault, an Algerian Frenchman who kills an Arab man on a beach.
Narrator and protagonist; emotionally detached, condemned more for his indifference than his crime.
The absurd — clash between human longing for meaning and a universe that offers none.
Famous opening line; the imperfect tense conveys uncertainty about timing.
Camus chose passé composé to create distance and immediacy.
European-origin colonial settler in French Algeria — Meursault's background.
